<reason>B more convincingly distinguished feasible reintroduction from justified imposition. A’s strongest attack concerned a disguised local veto, but B answered with an explicit approval process and a concrete case where opposition could be overridden. That concession gave A legitimate closing pressure, yet did not establish its broader prescription. B also supplied an immediate restoration alternative and challenged the continuing costs of coexistence. A never adequately resolved those comparisons, instead repeatedly portraying B’s approach as endless meetings and ecological abandonment.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal distinguished a self-sustaining predator population from a self-sustaining policy: fencing, guarding, compensation, and cooperation remain necessary. Combined with targeted browsing control protecting seedlings during delay, this substantially weakened A’s claimed choice between imposed predators and permanently deteriorating forests.</best_rebuttal>
